title: 育儿与教育：情绪教养基础 — Day 1
title_en: Parenting: Foundations of Emotion Coaching — Day 1

questions.question: 孩子的积木倒了，大哭尖叫。按「情绪命名」的思路，家长第一句话最该怎么说？
options: 「下次搭底下宽一点就不会倒了。」
「你气坏了，对吧？花了好久搭的，一下子全倒了。」
「别哭了别哭了，我们再搭一次就好，这次一定更高。」
「你又在发脾气了，这样可不好。」
questions.explanation: 用语言准确说出孩子的情绪本身就能降温，相关研究发现标注情绪时杏仁核活动下降。急着给解决方案时孩子还在情绪里听不进去；「你又在发脾气」虽然也点出情绪，但那是评判，命名应该是描述。
questions.question_en: A child's block tower collapses and they burst into screaming tears. Following the 'name it to tame it' approach, what should the parent say first?
options_en: 'Next time make the bottom wider and it won't fall.'
'You're so mad, aren't you? You worked on that for ages and it all fell down.'
'Don't cry, don't cry—we'll build it again, even taller this time.'
'You're throwing a tantrum again, and that's not okay.'
questions.explanation_en: Putting the child's feeling into accurate words is itself calming; research found that labeling emotions lowers amygdala activity. Jumping to solutions fails because the child is still flooded. 'You're throwing a tantrum again' names a feeling too, but as a judgment—labeling should describe, not condemn.

questions.question: 晚上该关 iPad 了，孩子还想看。哪种回应最符合权威型教养？
options: 今天先不管，等明天孩子心情好时再讲规则
先承认孩子想看完，再讲明关屏规则和理由，给一个有限选择
坚决要求立刻关掉，不做解释也不商量，规则就是规则，没得谈
看孩子这么想看，就再通融十分钟，避免冲突
questions.explanation: 权威型是高要求加高回应：温度和界限同时在场，再用有限选择给孩子自主感。只有规则没有温度是威权型，孩子学会服从但内化动机弱；只有温度没有界限是放任型，孩子学不会自我调节。
questions.question_en: It's time to turn off the iPad, but the child wants to keep watching. Which response best fits authoritative parenting?
options_en: Let it slide tonight and explain the rule tomorrow when the child is in a better mood
Acknowledge that the child wants to finish, state the 8:30 screens-off rule and why, then offer a limited choice
Insist it goes off right now—no explanation, no negotiation; rules are rules
Since the child wants it so badly, allow ten more minutes to avoid a fight
questions.explanation_en: Authoritative parenting means high demands plus high responsiveness: warmth and limits together, with a limited choice to preserve autonomy. Rules without warmth is authoritarian—children obey but internalize little; warmth without limits is permissive—children never learn to self-regulate.

questions.question: 孩子在超市哭闹打滚要买玩具。按 time-in 的做法，下面哪项描述正确？
options: 带孩子到安静处，答应买玩具让他尽快平静下来，回家再讲规则
到安静处陪着他，不讲道理也不答应要求，等情绪过去再谈
让孩子独自去角落冷静，等他想清楚了再回来认错
陪在孩子身边，趁他还在哭时耐心讲清楚为什么不能买
questions.explanation: Time-in 的要点是共同调节：孩子失控时前额叶离线，需要借大人平静的神经系统降温，所以要陪着而不是孤立。陪伴不等于奖励，不合理的要求依然不满足；情绪没下来时讲道理也进不去。
questions.question_en: A child is wailing and thrashing on the supermarket floor, demanding a toy. Which description of the 'time-in' approach is correct?
options_en: Take the child somewhere quiet and agree to buy the toy so they calm down fast, then explain the rule at home
Take the child somewhere quiet and stay with them—no lecturing and no giving in—then talk once the emotion has passed
Send the child to a corner alone to cool off and come back to apologize once they've thought it over
Stay beside the child and patiently explain, while they're still crying, why they can't have it
questions.explanation_en: Time-in is about co-regulation: a dysregulated child's prefrontal cortex is offline, so they need to borrow a calm adult's nervous system rather than be isolated. Staying close is not a reward—the unreasonable demand still goes unmet—and reasoning doesn't land until the emotion subsides.
